key_insight: Crystal VAE latent representations spontaneously cluster by elemental family, enabling FamilySpace to steer generated crystals toward user-specified family compositions.
engineering_relevance: Family-level composition control can focus materials discovery on promising chemical regions without reinforcement learning or additional optimization.
method: Identify elemental-family structure in atom-wise VAE latent representations.
Train a flow model with family-indexed source components and family-matched source–target pairs.
Use a user-defined family template to select the source component for each atom during generation.
evidence_signal: On MP-20 and MPTS-52, FamilySpace reports competitive generation performance and prescribed family-composition matching; selected templates increase the fraction predicted stable or metastable.
watch_item: Family-composition control does not guarantee exact elemental identities or experimental stability; reported stability gains are prediction-based and template-dependent.
paper_title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation
